title: Dispute: is venial sin against the law, or only beside it?
source_text: XXIV. Quaerunt autem hic Theologi Ecclesiae Romanae, An peccatum veniale sit contra Dei legem, An vero tantum praeter Dei legem. Et quidem sunt inter eos multi, qui existimant peccatum veniale non tam esse contra legem, quam praeter legem. Et in eo constituunt discrimen peccati mortalis & venialis, quod mortale sit contra legem, veniale solum praeter legem. Quae est Bellarmini sententia, lib. 1. de Amiss. Grat. & statu Peccati, cap. 11. in Explicatione quinti Argumenti. Alii vero censent tam veniale, quam mortale peccatum esse contra Dei legem. Quam sententiam tenet Vasquez, Tom. 1. in 1.2. Disput. 143. cap. 3.
pass_a_gloss: But here the theologians of the Roman Church ask whether venial sin is against God’s law, or truly only beside God’s law. And indeed there are many among them who judge that venial sin is not so much against the law as beside the law. And in that they establish the difference of mortal and venial sin, that mortal is against the law, venial only beside the law. Which is Bellarmine’s opinion, book 1 On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, chapter 11, in the Explanation of the fifth Argument. But others hold that venial as well as mortal sin is against God’s law. Which opinion Vasquez holds, Tom. 1 on 1a2ae, Disputation 143, chapter 3.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors split: Bellarmine’s camp sets venial ‘beside’ the law, mortal ‘against’ it.
Vasquez and others keep both venial and mortal as against God’s law.

choices.why: Bellarmine’s technical contrast with contra legem.
